finding: Binary and source confirmation of the mechanism the four-design decomposition located statistically: the leading-zero phase's dummy doubling is out of place, and the out-of-place path in eccProjectiveDblPoint copies three big integers the in-place path skips.
method: objdump -dr on the built crypto/libcrypt_s.a of each pinned MatrixSSL tree, per symbol, with addresses and relocation offsets normalised so two builds are comparable; plus the guarded copy read out of the source.

4-3-0-open eccMulmod (entry point after.note: a two-instruction thunk that jumps to the constant-time routine, which is what 'enabled by default' looks like in the binary: the old entry point no longer contains the old algorithm.

byte_identity: The normalised disassembly of eccMulmodCt is IDENTICAL between 4-3-0-open and 4-6-0-open (same 380 instructions, same digest of the normalised listing). The earlier reported 0.123 -> 0.084 movement between those releases was therefore run-to-run variation on the same code, and is retracted.

static_call_profile.note: The static call profile of 4-2-1 eccMulmod and 4-3-0 eccMulmodCt is identical, including 9 pstm_copy sites and 3 eccProjectiveAddPoint sites. The fix did not add or remove call sites; it changed which of them run and with what arguments. That is why a static diff alone cannot settle the mechanism and the dynamic decomposition was needed.

the_cost_asymmetry.dummy_path_source: ecc_math.c, mode==0 branches: eccProjectiveDblPoint(pool, M[1], M[2], ...) with P = M[1] and R = M[2], so P != R.
the_cost_asymmetry.real_path_source: ecc_math.c, accumulating branch: eccProjectiveDblPoint(pool, M[i], M[i], ...) with P = R, so P == R.
the_cost_asymmetry.the_guard: eccProjectiveDblPoint opens with `if (P != R) { pstm_copy(&P->x, &R->x); pstm_copy(&P->y, &R->y); pstm_copy(&P->z, &R->z); }`. The dummy path takes that branch and the real path does not, so each leading zero costs three extra big-integer copies. pstm_copy is variable time in the operand's `used` digit count, which is what makes an operation-count balance fail to be a cost balance.
